Jitendra Bahadur Chaurasia And Another vs Union Of India And
4 Others on 21 March, 2023
Author: Sunita Agarwal

Bench: Sunita Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 39
Case :- Writ - C No. - 32980 of 2021
Petitioner :- Jitendra Bahadur Chaurasia And Another
Respondent :- Union Of India And 4 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for Petitioner :- Om Prakash Chaurasia

Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,Akanksha Gaur,C.S.C.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
Heard Sri Om Prakash Chaurasia, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Neeraj Dubey, learned counsel, who appears for N.H.A.I.
The petitioner herein claims compensation based on the sale deed dated 25.02.1972, which was executed in the name of mother of the petitioner, namely, Smt.
Maheshwari Devi wife of Prabhu Nath by one Musafir Yadav son of Ram Nath Yadav, resident of Mauja Mardah Kanthwali, Post- Mardah Pachotar, Pargana and District Ghazipur.
It is stated in the writ petition that the tenure-holder of the plot in question had died in the year 1995 and the father of the petitioner had also died in 2006.
A house was constructed over the plot in question, wherein petitioner is living as on date without any dispute.

In the year 2015, the land as well as the house in question had been acquired for the purposes of National Highway (NH-29) and Jitendra Bahadur Chaurasia And Another vs Union Of India And 4 Others on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156182190/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: notice under Section 3-E of the National Highway Act, 1956 had been issued to all the concerned except the petitioner herein.
There exists room, shop and other constructions over the plot in question.

It is stated that the petitioner was waiting for disbursement of compensation, but the respondents had started demolition of the house of the petitioners and then an application dated 18.08.2021 was moved before the respondent seeking payment of compensation.
On a query made by the made about mutation of the name of the mother of the petitioners over the plot in question pursuant to the sale deed dated 25.02.1972, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that there has been no mutation.
The sale deed dated 25.02.1972 does not indicate the number of plot, which was sold in favour of the mother of the petitioners.

In the said scenario, it appears that the sale deed did not see the light of the day till the year 2021, inasmuch as the mother of the petitioners, the vendee, did not pursue her claim for mutation of her name over the plot in question.
It is, thus, difficult to ascertain the entitlement of the petitioner for acquisition in question.

For all disputed factual issues raised before us, the proper remedy for the petitioner is to file a suit before the Revenue Court seeking declaration of his right, title and interest over the land in question and only after identification of the land, subject matter of the sale deed dated 25.02.1972, there could arise a question for determination or payment of compensation.
No mandamus, at this stage, can be issued.
The writ petition is, accordingly, disposed off.
Order Date :- 21.3.2023 N.S.Rathour  Jitendra Bahadur Chaurasia And Another vs Union Of India And 4 Others on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156182190/
